newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-Canal Plus leaves Germany, bets on Italy.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Canal Plus leaves Germany, bets on Italy.

text.p: The board of Canal Plus on Wednesday effectively decided to leave Europe's biggest television market, Germany, and strengthen the company's position in Italy.

The company said in a statement after a meeting of the supervisory board that it would sell its 37.5 percent stake in German pay-television company Premiere to the Kirch Gruppe run by Bavarian meda mogul Leo Kirch.

Canal Plus said it would also buy a 45 percent stake in Italy's Telepiu from Kirch. The financial details of the transaction will not be made public until after the deal is finalised, expected in the next few days.

Canal Plus shares closed 0.17 percent higher at 1,209 in a steeply lower market. They had reached a year high earlier in the day at 1,245 francs. Analysts expect Kirch will have to pay an additional 900 million francs for the difference in value between the Premiere stake and the Telepiu stake.
The Premiere stake is valued at between 1.7 billion and 2.4 billion francs by analysts while the Telepiu stake is estimated to be worth between 1.3 billion and 1.4 billion.
The deal had long been expected and marks a peace treaty in what has been a fierce battle in the European pay televison scene which raged in the last two years.
Canal Plus, Kirch and Bertelsmann each had a one third stake in Premiere, the biggest pay television group in Germany.
But the companies fell out when Canal Plus and Bertelsmann wanted to set up a digital satellite television service in Germany, using Premiere as a launch pad.

They even wanted Kirch to sell out so that Rupert Murdoch's BSkyB could enter Premiere. Kirch had a rival digital satellite plan. But after a number of deals, rows and marriages worthy of a soap opera, Bertelsmann ditched its digital satellite ambitions and married its television unit UFA with Luxembourg's CLT. Canal Plus then merged with Nethold, a pay-televison group contro
By leaving Germany, Canal Plus now has a lead position in France in pay television and satellite television although it is rivalled by the TPS grouping of TF1, France Television and CLT.
In Italy it is master of Telepiu and it has lead positions in Poland and Scandinavia. It was the market leader in Spain but has run into flak from the new government there.

Canal Plus has complained with the European Commission that Spain's requirement for a specific type of decoding was effectively barring its Canalsatellite unit from operating in the country. Spain has asked the European Commission for advice on the matter.
